projects.title: Flow State
projects.subtitle: Dictation that fits into a macOS workflow
projects.problem: Dictation is useful only if the text ends up where you are working. Flow State brings speech recognition into the current application instead of making the user move between a recorder and an editor.
projects.contribution: I built the macOS application in Swift, using SwiftUI for the interface and AppKit for integration with the desktop. A global shortcut starts the workflow, WhisperKit handles local transcription, and the result can be inserted into the active application.
projects.engineering_detail: The local code separates transcription behind a provider interface, allowing the application to select a backend without putting model-specific logic throughout the interface. Optional Groq formatting adapts the text to its destination.
projects.limitations: WhisperKit handles transcription on the Mac. Optional Groq formatting sends the transcript to an external service; users can choose whether to enable it.

projects.title: Prepify interview analysis backend
projects.subtitle: Keeping analysis work out of the request cycle
projects.role: Backend contributor on a team project
projects.problem: An interview analysis request can involve several stages of audio and video processing. Doing that work inside a single web request would make the user wait for the entire pipeline before receiving a response.
projects.contribution: I built FastAPI endpoints that create PostgreSQL job records, queue interview analysis through Celery and RabbitMQ, and return HTTP 202 with a job ID. I also wrote automated tests and technical documentation for the backend.
projects.engineering_detail: The worker retrieves interview video from AWS S3, retries unavailable downloads up to 12 times, and falls back to audio-only analysis when needed. Job state, results and errors are stored in PostgreSQL; worker logs help trace failures while the application polls for progress.
projects.limitations: Prepify is a team project. This page focuses on my backend contribution. I have not published throughput or production reliability benchmarks.

projects.title: Phoneme Error Detection
projects.subtitle: Making pronunciation feedback easier to use
projects.role: Dashboard contributor on a team project
projects.problem: A transcript can show which word a system recognized, but it does not explain which sound a learner should practice. This team project analyzes speech at the phoneme level and presents feedback in a practice interface.
projects.contribution: I contributed an adaptive pronunciation dashboard. The application lets users record a word, view analysis results, and revisit saved attempts. My contribution is part of a larger system with a FastAPI backend and a Wav2Vec2-based phoneme model.
projects.engineering_detail: The backend compares predicted phonemes with a reference pronunciation and returns a structured response for the interface. Separate history endpoints let the product retain attempts instead of treating each recording as an isolated result.
projects.limitations: This was a team-built application. My contribution was the adaptive dashboard and practice workflow; the speech model was part of the broader team project.

projects.title: EchoPath
projects.subtitle: Exploring camera-based spatial audio cues
projects.problem: EchoPath explores whether a camera and headphones can communicate useful information about nearby objects. It translates visual observations into directional tones and spoken cues.
projects.contribution: I developed a local prototype that combines YOLO object detection, Depth Anything V2 depth estimates, object tracking, and spatial audio. The implementation can use OpenAL for spatialization, with a stereo audio fallback.
projects.engineering_detail: Raw detections can change from frame to frame. The tracking layer associates boxes over time and smooths estimated nearness before updating the sound. Spoken announcements use cooldowns so an object does not trigger the same message continuously.
projects.limitations: This is a prototype, not a validated navigation aid. Monocular depth estimates are relative signals, not a guarantee of physical distance. A usable mobility system would need careful testing with its intended users, including failures and environmental changes.

projects.title: Sync Assignments
projects.subtitle: Turning course emails into tasks
projects.problem: Assignment notices arrive in email, while the work is planned in a calendar or task manager. Copying the same deadlines into another system is repetitive and easy to get wrong.
projects.contribution: I built a Python workflow that reads course email notices, extracts assignments, and synchronizes them with Google Tasks and Todoist. The local version also includes a macOS launcher and notifications.
projects.engineering_detail: The workflow handles existing entries and daily-run checks rather than blindly adding a new task on every run. It reports new and existing assignments and sends a completion or error notification.
projects.limitations: The workflow depends on the structure of course email notices and the connected task services.

projects.title: MediScribe capstone
projects.subtitle: Adding anomaly alerts to a healthcare application
projects.problem: The capstone explores healthcare data workflows through transcription, dashboards, and analysis. One part of the work focuses on making cross-hospital anomalies visible to a reviewer.
projects.contribution: I contributed cross-hospital anomaly detection and hospital alerts to the team’s MediScribe capstone. My work focused on surfacing unusual patterns for review within the larger healthcare application.
projects.engineering_detail: The alert feature connects analysis results to a reviewer-facing workflow. It sits alongside transcription and dashboard components built by the team.
projects.limitations: This was an academic team project, separate from my MIE internship. The alerts were not clinically validated.

projects.title: Purchase price variance dashboard
projects.subtitle: From weekly file preparation to part-level investigation
projects.problem: A weekly report depended on one colleague spending roughly three to four hours preparing and consolidating source data. Other people had to wait for that step before reviewing purchase price variance.
projects.contribution: I built a source-file consolidation pipeline and integrated it into a dashboard used by the sourcing team. Users can move from a global view to a commodity, buyer, supplier, organization, or individual part.
projects.engineering_detail: Exception reporting highlights records that need investigation, including parts with a zero standard cost. The same interface shows favorable and unfavorable variance and progress against goals.
projects.result: The consolidation step runs in under 30 seconds. Exception reporting surfaces approximately 10–15 parts per month for investigation and correction.
projects.limitations: These figures describe the internal workflow I worked on. Consolidation time excludes subsequent investigation and review.

projects.title: Supplier forecast automation
projects.subtitle: Generate the workbooks, then make review straightforward
projects.problem: Preparing and validating individual supplier forecasts could take two to three weeks. A readiness assessment also surfaced gaps in regular forecast communication.
projects.contribution: I built a tool that takes the supplier list and source data, generates each supplier’s Excel forecast in horizontal and vertical layouts, and prepares Outlook drafts with the right recipients and copied contacts.
projects.engineering_detail: Generation and sending are separate steps. The tool prepares the files and drafts; people validate the output before sending it. That keeps the monthly communication process reviewable.
projects.result: Workbook generation takes under a minute, followed by a few hours of validation. The team adopted the workflow for monthly forecasts.
projects.limitations: The full process includes human validation and sending. The tool is not described as sending forecasts autonomously.

projects.title: Supplier readiness assessment
projects.subtitle: Find where a production ramp needs more preparation
projects.role: Developer and analyst at Brooks Automation
projects.problem: Ahead of a production ramp, the sourcing team needed a consistent way to understand supplier readiness and decide where to focus follow-up.
projects.contribution: I built a survey sent to about 80 suppliers and tools that process the responses into a readiness view. The team can identify lagging suppliers and direct commodity managers to the areas that need attention.
projects.engineering_detail: The workflow connects supplier responses to a repeatable review process, so the team can run the assessment again rather than rebuild the analysis each time.
projects.result: The survey and analysis became a recurring team process.
projects.limitations: About 80 refers to suppliers sent the survey. It is not a claim about response rate or improved delivery performance.

projects.title: On-time delivery intelligence
projects.subtitle: Explore global delivery data and possible disruption
projects.role: Developer during an IT internship at Brooks Automation
projects.problem: Teams needed a common view of delivery performance and a way to investigate gaps across suppliers and shipments.
projects.contribution: I built the dashboard and data workflow, combining unstructured source data into a global delivery view with drill-down. I also added news-based exploration of possible disruption and a conversational agent for questions and report generation.
projects.engineering_detail: The news feature helps users explore which suppliers or shipments may be exposed to an event. The conversational interface gives another way to work with the underlying delivery data and prepare reports.
projects.result: I demonstrated the system across teams, including to the CIO and sourcing leadership.
projects.limitations: The news feature helps people investigate potential exposure. It is not an automated decision to reroute shipments or change suppliers.
